w:r.w:t: This document consolidates the written deliverables that can be prepared from the assignment instructions and the supplied professional resume. The assignment requires a GitHub repository, feature branch, issue, incremental commits, AI-use record, human review, testing evidence, pull request, merge, GitHub Pages deployment, and reflection. The written materials below are prepared; repository-specific URLs, screenshots, commit IDs, and live deployment results must be inserted after the actual GitHub workflow is performed.
`human-code-review.md` prepared; exact paths/results require repository inspection

The assignment asks the student to use a public professional resume/profile as a content source, create public-facing content notes, customize an instructor-approved portfolio template, and use AI as a directed coding assistant. The emphasis is on directing, inspecting, testing, revising, and taking responsibility for AI-assisted software work.

The assignment specifically requires a content-notes.md file, at least five observable acceptance criteria, a GitHub issue, a feature branch named feature/portfolio-personalization, an AI plan before implementation, at least three meaningful commits, human review, repeatable testing, a pull request, a merge, GitHub Pages publication, live-site verification, and a reflection issue.
The supplied resume supports the following public professional identity:
Senior Financial Analyst — Asset Liability Management
M.S. in Artificial Intelligence, concentration in Machine Learning, University of Michigan–Flint, expected April 2028, GPA 4.00/4.00
B.S. in Actuarial Mathematics, University of Michigan–Flint, April 2016, GPA 3.3/4.00
Interests: data science, predictive modeling, AI/ML, financial risk analytics, asset liability management, Azure SQL Server, Bloomberg MARS

Privacy decision: the resume contains a street address, phone number, and personal email address. Those fields are deliberately excluded from public portfolio content. This follows the assignment's requirement that content-notes.md contain only information the student is comfortable publishing.
Landing page displays name and concise ALM/financial-analytics role.
Load home page and visually confirm.
Experience and Education sections use verified resume information.
Narrow mobile viewport remains readable and usable.
Use a narrow responsive viewport; check for overflow/overlap.
No private contact information or template placeholders remain.
External/project links are real or omitted if unverifiable.
Keyboard navigation and image alternative text are usable.
Tab through controls; inspect alt text.
Reload and navigate while watching the console.
Title: Build and publish my AI-assisted portfolio update

Problem statement: Customize the instructor-approved static portfolio template into a professional public portfolio using verified resume information while preserving the template's attribution/license and avoiding private information.
Audience: internship/recruiting reviewers, software/AI/data reviewers, and financial-risk technology professionals.
Non-goals: backend, database, login/authentication, analytics, and external data collection.

Major checklist: fork repository; add README/content notes; create issue; create feature branch; plan with AI; implement incrementally; review; test; open PR; merge; enable Pages; verify live site; complete reflection.
Commit 1 — Add initial portfolio content and project issue
Commit 2 — Update portfolio identity and navigation
Commit 3 — Add education, experience, skills, and interests
Commit 4 — Improve responsive layout and accessibility (optional extra commit if useful)
The assignment requires at least three meaningful commits. Each commit should represent a coherent, reviewable change rather than an uncontrolled repository rewrite.

The prepared AI prompt tells the assistant the project purpose, existing static architecture, allowed files/changes, acceptance criteria, privacy/accessibility constraints, prohibited additions, and the requirement to provide a plan, assumptions/risks, tests, and questions before editing.

The recommended plan is to inspect the starter structure first, update identity/navigation, add verified experience and education content, make focused responsive/accessibility corrections, update documentation, and test the resulting diff and rendered site.
Incremental file-by-file changes and acceptance-criteria-driven implementation.
Do not add project/external links unless a real destination can be verified; the resume does not supply project URLs.
Longer resume content may expose responsive-layout problems.
Private resume contact information could be copied to a public site; this was addressed by creating a filtered public-content source.
Compared all factual claims with content-notes.md; checked for invented credentials.
Clicked each navigation item and checked destination IDs.
Adjust only selectors causing observed issues.
Correct any mismatch with final repo.

The assignment requires local or repository-preview testing, plus screenshots or a short recording for at least three tests. These must be performed against the actual customized repository rather than assumed.
☐ External/project links work, or the test is marked N/A when no unverifiable links were added.
☐ Images have meaningful alternative text or are decorative.
☐ No secrets or private data are exposed.
☐ Browser console has no unexplained errors.
Evidence 1: normal-width page load and identity/experience content screenshot.
Evidence 3: navigation/accessibility/console test screenshot or short recording.

Summary: This pull request customizes the starter static portfolio into a professional portfolio for Christian Benjamin Namath Heiney, using verified resume information and focused responsive/accessibility changes.
Acceptance criteria checklist: include all eight criteria and mark them after testing.
Testing performed: include the completed test table.
AI assistance: planning, content transformation, implementation assistance, accessibility/responsive suggestions.
Known limitations: no private contact information; no backend/login/analytics; no unverifiable project links.

After merge, GitHub Pages should be configured to deploy from the default branch and repository root, then verified using the live URL. The assignment explicitly requires testing the published result rather than relying only on local behavior.
Pages deployment evidence: CAPTURE AFTER DEPLOYMENT
The feature branch and pull request workflow were most useful because they separated AI-assisted work from the default branch and provided a clear review checkpoint.
The incremental implementation suggestion was accepted because smaller changes are easier to inspect, test, and revert. Acceptance-criteria mapping also made the review objective.

The AI could not decide solely from the resume which information was safe to publish. Private contact information was therefore excluded through a filtered content-notes.md source. Unverifiable project URLs were also excluded rather than invented.
The workflow demonstrated that generation is only one step. The engineer remains responsible for requirements, factual accuracy, privacy, accessibility, testing, and the decision to publish.

A second iteration could add verified technical projects. The value would be stronger evidence of AI/ML and software ability; the risks are unsupported claims and accidental disclosure. Verified repositories/demos and accurate contribution descriptions would be required first.
